questions.question: A girl goes to school at a speed of 20 km/h. She comes back with a speed of 12 km/h. Find her average speed for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For equal forward and return distances, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 20 × 12) ÷ (20 + 12)

⇒ Average Speed = 480 ÷ 32

⇒ Average Speed = 15 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Home
 
 School
 
• 
 

 Speed = 20 km/h
 
• 
 

 Speed = 12 km/h
 
• 
 Constant Distance (D)

**Given:**

Speed to school (S₁) = 20 km/h

Speed returning (S₂) = 12 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

Let the distance between home and school be the LCM of speeds 20 and 12, which is 60 km.

⇒ Time taken to reach school = Distance ÷ S₁ = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 hours

⇒ Time taken to return = Distance ÷ S₂ = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 hours

⇒ Total Distance for the round trip = 60 + 60 = 120 km

⇒ Total Time taken = 3 + 5 = 8 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 120 ÷ 8

⇒ Average Speed = 15 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 15 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

When a person travels three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, the Average Speed = (3xyz) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Average Speed with Equal Time Intervals

When a person travels at speed S₁ for time T and speed S₂ for the same duration T, the Average Speed = (S₁ + S₂) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, their Relative Speed = (S₁ − S₂). When moving in opposite directions, their Relative Speed = (S₁ + S₂).

questions.question: If the fourth proportion to 17, X and 7 is 91, then find the value of X.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion, the product of means equals the product of extremes.

b × c = a × d

X × 7 = 17 × 91

X = (17 × 91) ÷ 7 = 17 × 13

X = 221

**∴ The correct answer is 221.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers 17, X, 7, and 91 are in proportion.

**Formula Used:**

For values a, b, c, d in proportion: a ÷ b = c ÷ d

questions.question: A pen is purchased for ₹40 and sold for ₹50. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Cost Price to Selling Price = 40 : 50 = 4 : 5

Profit = 5 − 4 = 1 part

Profit % = (Profit parts ÷ Cost Price parts) × 100

Profit % = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 CP = ₹40
 
 
 SP = ₹50
 
 

 

 
 + ₹10 (Profit)

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the pen = ₹40

Selling Price (SP) of the pen = ₹50

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit = 50 − 40

⇒ Profit = ₹10

⇒ Profit % = (10 ÷ 40) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (1 ÷ 4) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Cost Price (CP) > Selling Price (SP), a loss is incurred. Loss = CP − SP. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the effective combined discount is given by the formula: [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.

questions.question: In an examination there are 150 questions and 4 marks are given for every correct answer and 1 mark is deducted for every wrong answer. A candidate attempted all 150 questions and scored 250 marks. Find the number of questions he answered correctly.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let correct = x ⇒ wrong = 150 − x

Total marks = 4x − (150 − x)

= 5x − 150

5x − 150 = 250 ⇒ x = 80

**∴ Answer = 80**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total questions = 150, +4 for correct, −1 for wrong, total score = 250

**Formula used:**

Total score = (correct × 4) − (wrong × 1)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let correct answers = x

⇒ Wrong answers = 150 − x

⇒ Score = 4x − (150 − x)

⇒ = 4x − 150 + x = 5x − 150

⇒ 5x − 150 = 250

⇒ 5x = 400

⇒ x = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Scoring System

Total score = (marks for correct) − (penalty for wrong)

Linear Equation

Form equation using total questions and score

Shortcut Insight

Each question effectively contributes +5 when switching wrong to correct

questions.question: Two trains are running on parallel tracks towards each other. Train A is 250 meters long and is moving at a speed of 90 km/h. Train B is 150 meters long and is moving at a speed of 60 km/h. How much time (rounded off to the nearest seconds) will it take for Train A to completely pass Train B?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Opposite direction ⇒ add speeds

Total distance = 250 + 150 = 400 m

Relative speed = 90 + 60 = 150 km/h = 41.67 m/s

Time = 400 ÷ 41.67 ≈ 9.6 sec

**∴ Answer = 10 seconds**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of A = 250 m, Length of B = 150 m

Speed of A = 90 km/h, Speed of B = 60 km/h

**Formula used:**

Time = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total distance = 250 + 150 = 400 m

⇒ Relative speed = 90 + 60 = 150 km/h

⇒ Convert speed = 150 × (5/18) = 41.67 m/s

⇒ Time = 400 ÷ 41.67 ≈ 9.6 sec

⇒ Rounded off = 10 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 10 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

Opposite direction ⇒ speeds are added

Unit Conversion

km/h to m/s ⇒ multiply by 5/18

Train Rule

Total distance = sum of lengths

questions.question: The monthly incomes of two friends Manjit and Keshav are in the ratio 5 : 9 respectively and each of them saves ₹48,000 every month. If the ratio of their monthly expenditure is 1 : 3, then find the monthly income of Manjit (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the Cross-Multiplication Method for identical savings of ₹48,000:

Ratio cross-product difference = (5 × 3) − (9 × 1) = 15 − 9 = 6 units.

Savings cross-product difference = (3 × 48000) − (1 × 48000) = 96000.

⇒ 6 units = 96000 ⇒ 1 unit = 16000.

⇒ Manjit's Income = 5 units = 5 × 16000 = 80000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹80,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Manjit Keshav Income Expenditure Savings 5 9 1 3 48000 48000 
• 
• 
• 
• 15 − 9 = 6 units 144k − 48k = 96,000 
• ⇒ 6 units = 96,000 ⇒ 1 unit = 16,000 Manjit's Income = 5 × 16,000 = ₹80,000 

**Given:**

Ratio of monthly incomes of Manjit and Keshav = 5 : 9

Ratio of their monthly expenditure = 1 : 3

Savings of each = ₹48,000

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

**Calculation:**

Let the monthly incomes of Manjit and Keshav be 5x and 9x respectively.

⇒ Expenditure of Manjit = 5x − 48000

⇒ Expenditure of Keshav = 9x − 48000

According to the given condition:

⇒ (5x − 48000) ÷ (9x − 48000) = 1 ÷ 3

Cross-multiplying the equation:

⇒ 3 × (5x − 48000) = 1 × (9x − 48000)

⇒ 15x − 144000 = 9x − 48000

⇒ 15x − 9x = 144000 − 48000

⇒ 6x = 96000

⇒ x = 16000

Now, calculating Manjit's monthly income:

⇒ Manjit's income = 5x = 5 × 16000 = 80000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹80,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income & Expenditure Relation

The foundational equation for all such problems is: Income = Expenditure + Savings. Changes in any one aspect proportionally affect the others.

Cross-Multiplication Shortcut

When initial quantities are increased or decreased to form a new ratio, equating the cross-product difference of the ratios to the cross-product difference of the changes quickly yields the value of one unit.

Alternative Gap Balancing

If the savings for both individuals are identical, you can also multiply the ratios by suitable constants to make the horizontal differences between corresponding terms equal, directly revealing the exact unit value without applying any variables.

questions.question: If a² - b² = 21 and a - b = 3 , what is a + b ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the algebraic identity for the difference of squares:

a + b = (a² − b²) ÷ (a − b)

Substitute the given values directly:

⇒ a + b = 21 ÷ 3 = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a² − b² = 21

a − b = 3

**Formula Used:**

x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y)

**Calculations:**

Applying the formula to the given variables:

⇒ a² − b² = 21

⇒ (a − b)(a + b) = 21

Substitute the given value of (a − b):

⇒ 3 × (a + b) = 21

⇒ a + b = 21 ÷ 3

⇒ a + b = 7

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Identities

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² 
 (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²

Sum and Difference of Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) 
 a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

Cube of a Sum and Difference

(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b) 
 (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b)

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 90 cm, 11 cm and 97 cm. What is the length of its altitude corresponding to the side with the length of 11 cm?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sides = 90, 11, 97

s = (90 + 11 + 97)/2 = 99

Area = √[99×9×88×2] = √156816 = 396

Altitude = (2×Area)/base = (2×396)/11

**∴ Answer = 72 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides = 90 cm, 11 cm, 97 cm

**Formula used:**

Heron’s formula: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)]

Altitude = (2 × Area) / base

**Calculation:**

⇒ s = (90 + 11 + 97)/2 = 99

⇒ Area = √[99(99−90)(99−11)(99−97)]

⇒ = √[99 × 9 × 88 × 2]

⇒ = √156816 = 396

⇒ Altitude on side 11 = (2 × 396) / 11

⇒ = 792 / 11 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron’s Formula

Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)]

Altitude Formula

Height = (2 × Area) / base

Triangle Check

Sum of any two sides must be greater than third

questions.question: The present ages of Rohit and his father are in the ratio 2 : 5. Four years from now, the ratio of their ages will become 12 : 27. What was the father's age (in years) five years ago from now?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let present ages = 2x, 5x

After 4 years ⇒ (2x+4)/(5x+4) = 12/27 = 4/9

⇒ 9(2x+4) = 4(5x+4)

⇒ 18x + 36 = 20x + 16 ⇒ x = 10

Father’s present age = 5x = 50

**∴ Age 5 years ago = 45**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present ratio = 2 : 5

Future ratio (after 4 years) = 12 : 27

**Formula used:**

Form linear equation using ratios

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let present ages be 2x and 5x

⇒ After 4 years: (2x + 4)/(5x + 4) = 12/27

⇒ Simplify: 12/27 = 4/9

⇒ 9(2x + 4) = 4(5x + 4)

⇒ 18x + 36 = 20x + 16

⇒ 2x = 20 ⇒ x = 10

⇒ Father’s present age = 5x = 50

⇒ 5 years ago = 50 − 5 = 45

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Age Problems

Use variables to represent present ages

Ratio Simplification

Reduce ratios to simplest form before solving

questions.question: The cost price of a whiteboard is ₹2,800. The shopkeeper gave 87% of discount on the cost price. What is the selling price (in ₹)?

Since the discount is 87% directly on the Cost Price, the Selling Price will be the remaining percentage of the Cost Price.

Standard Discount Rule

Normally, discounts are given on the Marked Price (MP). So, SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100. However, as explicitly stated in this question, if the discount is calculated on Cost Price (CP), we apply the same logic on CP instead.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of x% and y% are given back to back, the single equivalent discount % = x + y − (x × y ÷ 100).

Profit and Loss Calculation

Profit % or Loss % is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specified otherwise. Profit = SP − CP, and Loss = CP − SP.

questions.question: {Evaluate: } sqrt{250 + sqrt{19 + sqrt{289}}} + sqrt{620 + sqrt{11 + sqrt{196}}}
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Solve the nested square roots step-by-step starting from the innermost to the outermost.

First part: √289 = 17 → √(19 + 17) = √36 = 6 → √(250 + 6) = √256 = 16

Second part: √196 = 14 → √(11 + 14) = √25 = 5 → √(620 + 5) = √625 = 25

Final sum = 16 + 25 = 41

**∴ The correct answer is 41.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

√(250 + √(19 + √289)) + √(620 + √(11 + √196))

**Calculations:**

⇒ Solve the innermost square roots first: √289 = 17 and √196 = 14

⇒ Substitute these values back into the expression:

⇒ √(250 + √(19 + 17)) + √(620 + √(11 + 14))

⇒ Simplify the addition inside the remaining inner roots:

⇒ √(250 + √36) + √(620 + √25)

⇒ Solve the next set of square roots: √36 = 6 and √25 = 5

⇒ Substitute these values back into the outermost roots:

⇒ √(250 + 6) + √(620 + 5)

⇒ Simplify the addition:

⇒ √256 + √625

⇒ Solve the final outermost square roots: √256 = 16 and √625 = 25

⇒ 16 + 25 = 41

**∴ The correct answer is 41.**

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Always follow the order of Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction when simplifying arithmetic expressions.

Nested Square Roots

When simplifying continuous or nested radicals, always start evaluating from the innermost root and work your way outwards step-by-step until the outermost root is solved.

Perfect Squares 1 to 30

Memorizing squares up to 30 (e.g., 14² = 196, 16² = 256, 17² = 289, 25² = 625) significantly increases your calculation speed in simplification and number system problems.
</p

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 50 and their LCM is 429. The two numbers are:2607
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can solve this quickly by testing the given options directly.

All pairs given in the options have a sum of 50, so we check their LCM.

For Option 1 (11 and 39), they share no common factors, making them co-prime.

The LCM of co-prime numbers is exactly their product ⇒ 11 × 39 = 429.

**∴ The correct answer is 11, 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two numbers = 50

LCM of the two numbers = 429

**Formula Used:**

If HCF of two numbers is H, they can be written as Hx and Hy (where x and y are co-prime).

Sum = H(x + y) and LCM = H × x × y

A quadratic equation with roots x and y is represented as: t² − (Sum)t + (Product) = 0

**Calculation:**

⇒ H must be a common factor of both the sum (50) and the LCM (429).

⇒ Prime factorization: 50 = 2 × 5² and 429 = 3 × 11 × 13.

⇒ The only common factor between 50 and 429 is 1, so H = 1.

⇒ Thus, the numbers are x and y, where x + y = 50 and x × y = 429.

⇒ Substitute the Sum and Product into the quadratic formula format.

⇒ t² − 50t + 429 = 0

⇒ t² − 11t − 39t + 429 = 0

⇒ t(t − 11) − 39(t − 11) = 0

⇒ (t − 11)(t − 39) = 0

⇒ The roots are t = 11 and t = 39.

**∴ The correct answer is 11, 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. Formula: a × b = HCF × LCM.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime if their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is exactly 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers will always be equal to their direct product.

Quadratic Equation Roots

If the sum of two numbers is S and their product is P, these two numbers represent the exact roots of the quadratic equation: x² − Sx + P = 0.
</p

questions.question: The average of the marks of 12 students in a class is 36. If the marks of each student are doubled, find the new average?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the properties of averages, if every observation in a dataset is multiplied by a constant, the new average is the original average multiplied by that same constant.

Given original average = 36.

Since the marks of each student are doubled, the average will also be doubled directly.

New Average = 36 × 2 = 72.

**∴ The correct answer is 72 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of students = 12

Average marks of the students = 36

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

 
 Avg = 36
 12 Students
 
 
• 
 

 × 2
 
 
 Avg = 72
 12 Students

 New Average = Old Avg × 2

**Calculations:**

⇒ Original sum of marks = Average × Number of students

⇒ Original sum of marks = 36 × 12 = 432

⇒ Since each student's marks are doubled, the new sum of marks will be twice the original sum.

⇒ New sum of marks = 432 × 2 = 864

⇒ New average = New sum ÷ Total number of students

⇒ New average = 864 ÷ 12 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 marks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition / Subtraction Property of Averages

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from each observation in a dataset, the average increases or decreases by that exact same value. Formula: New Avg = Old Avg ± k.

Multiplication / Division Property of Averages

If each observation is multiplied or divided by a non-zero constant 'k', the new average will be the old average multiplied or divided by 'k'. Formula: New Avg = Old Avg × k.

Combined Average

When two groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ have individual averages of A₁ and A₂ respectively, their overall combined average is calculated as: (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p
